See also: Chevalier

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle English chivaler or chevaler (also shyvalere while code-switching), from Anglo-Norman chevaler or chivaler, later refashioned after French chevalier, from Late Latin caballārius (“horseman”), from Latin caballus (“horse”).[1] Doublet of caballero and cavalier.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˌʃɛvəˈlɪɚ/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɪə(ɹ)

Noun

[edit]

chevalier (plural chevaliers)

  1. (historical) cavalier; knight
  2. (card games) In tarot cards, the card between the valet and the dame.

Related terms

[edit]
  • preux chevalier

Translations

[edit]
knight — see knight

References

[edit]
  1. ^ “chevalier”, in OED Online ⁠, Oxford: Oxford University Press, launched 2000.

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French chevalier, from Old French chevalier, from Late Latin caballārius, from Latin caballus. Doublet of cavalier.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ʃə.va.lje/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -je

Noun

[edit]

chevalier m (plural chevaliers, feminine chevalière)

  1. knight
  2. sandpiper (bird)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • chevaleresse
  • chevalier blanc
  • chevalier cuivré
  • chevalier de la manchette
  • chevalier de la rosette
  • chevalier d'honneur
  • chevalier d'industrie
  • chevalier du guet
  • chevalier errant
  • chevalier servant

Related terms

[edit]
  • cheval
  • chevaleresque
  • chevalerie
  • chevalin
  • chevaucher

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Ottoman Turkish: شوالیه (şövalye)
    • Turkish: şövalye
  • → Persian: شوالیه (šovâliye)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “chevalier”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from chevalier, from the fact that knights used to carry these rings as a seal. First attested in 1992.

Noun

[edit]

chevalier m (invariable)

  1. a ring that is flat on top and typically decorated with precious gems

Middle English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

chevalier

  1. alternative form of chivaler

Middle French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • shyvalere

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French chevalier.

Noun

[edit]

chevalier m (plural chevaliers)

  1. knight

Related terms

[edit]
  • cheval

Descendants

[edit]
  • French: chevalier
    • → Ottoman Turkish: شوالیه (şövalye)
      • Turkish: şövalye
    • → Persian: شوالیه (šovâliye)
  • Norman: quevalier

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cevalier (Picard)
  • chevaler, chivaler (Anglo-Norman)

Etymology

[edit]

From Late Latin caballārius, from Latin caballus.[1] Compare Old Occitan cavalier.

Noun

[edit]

chevalier oblique singular, m (oblique plural chevaliers, nominative singular chevaliers, nominative plural chevalier)

  1. knight
  2. (chess) knight

Descendants

[edit]
  • Middle French: chevalier, shyvalere
    • French: chevalier
      • → Ottoman Turkish: شوالیه (şövalye)
        • Turkish: şövalye
      • → Persian: شوالیه (šovâliye)
    • Norman: quevalier
    • Picard: cvalier
    • Bourguignon: chevaulei
  • → Middle English: chivaler, chevaler, chevalere, chevalier, chevaller, chevelere, chyvaler, chyvalour
    • English: chevalier (remodelled after modern French)

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Migliorini, Bruno with Aldo Duro (1950), “cavaliere”, in Prontuario etimologico della lingua italiana (in Italian), Paravia
